title: Offline bundle manifest schema (v0 draft)
content:
Context
- This doc is a working v0 schema draft for the offline bundle manifest used by Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem / air-gapped).
- The manifest is the primary signed payload; installers verify signature + hashes before proceeding (fail closed by default).
- Goal: deterministic, stable signatures across build environments, and enough metadata to:
  (1) verify integrity of every offline artifact
  (2) prevent replay/downgrade
  (3) support triage (support bundle / inspect command)

Non-goals for v0
- Full customer-signed bundles / delegated roots (future phase)
- Comprehensive SBOM schema (we will link/point to SBOM artifacts, not embed huge SBOM docs)
- Full provenance attestation format (SLSA-style). We’ll keep room for future extension.

File placement + naming (bundle layout assumption)
- Bundle root contains:
  - manifest.json (this file)
  - manifest.sig (detached signature; envelope discussed separately)
  - artifacts/… (charts, binaries, model/runtime artifacts)
  - images/… (optional: image tarballs) OR a local OCI registry seed directory
  - sbom/… (optional)

Manifest format overview
- Format is JSON for signing. We may optionally generate a human-readable YAML view for operators, but signature verification must operate on a canonical JSON representation.
- Fields are split into:
  - identity + versioning
  - build metadata (determinism + traceability)
  - compatibility and policy
  - artifact inventory (hashes + sizes)
  - optional SBOM references

Schema (v0) — field list and semantics

Top-level required fields
- manifest_format_version (string)
  - Example: "0.1"
  - Semver-ish for schema; not tied to Redwood product version.
- bundle_id (string)
  - Globally unique identifier for this bundle build.
  - Proposed format: "rbp_<yyyyMMdd>_<shortgit>_<buildnum>" or UUID.
- product (string)
  - Always "redwood-private" for now.
- product_version (string)
  - Redwood Private release version the bundle corresponds to.
  - Example: "2026.01.0" (match release tagging in release train).
- build (string)
  - Build identifier from CI, used for reproducibility and support correlation.
  - Example: "releases/private/2026.01.0+build.1842".
- created_at (string)
  - ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.
  - Example: "2026-01-05T18:42:11Z".

Compatibility + policy (required for v0)
- requires_installer
  - Field values are strings for v0 to keep parsing simple; we can upgrade to structured constraints later.
  - requires_installer_version (string)
    - Example: ">=1.19.0".
  - requires_installer_features (string)
    - Comma-separated features that must exist (e.g., "verify-signature,trust-store,downgrade-prevention").
- upgrade_policy (string)
  - Summary string for operators.
  - Example: "no-downgrade; install allowed from 2025.12.x -> 2026.01.x".
- minimum_supported_product_version (string)
  - Used for downgrade prevention.
  - Example: "2025.12.0".

Artifact inventory (required for v0)
- artifacts (list)
  - Each entry describes a file expected to exist in the offline bundle and to be hashed and verified.
  - For v0, each artifact entry MUST include:
    - logical_name (string) — stable handle used in logs/UI
    - relative_path (string) — path from bundle root using forward slashes
    - artifact_type (string) — one of: "installer", "helm_chart", "k8s_manifest", "runtime", "model", "dependency", "image_tar", "config", "sbom", "other"
    - sha256 (string) — lowercase hex
    - size_bytes (string) — numeric string (avoid 64-bit parsing issues across langs)
    - content_type (string) — MIME-like hint (e.g., "application/gzip")
  - Optional per artifact:
    - mode (string) — posix-style file mode as octal string (e.g., "0755") if we care about executability
    - platform (string) — e.g., "linux/amd64"
    - version (string) — chart/app/model version
    - source (string) — where it came from (internal build, vendor, upstream)

Container image inventory (optional in v0, but recommended)
- images (list)
  - If the bundle contains OCI image tarballs or pre-seeded registry content, we should still inventory the images expected.
  - Proposed required fields per image:
    - name (string) — e.g., "registry.redwood.example/redwood/control-plane"
    - digest (string) — e.g., "sha256:<hex>" (digest of the image manifest)
    - tags (string) — comma-separated list of tags shipped
    - source (string) — e.g., "redwood-release", "third-party"
  - Note: if images are shipped as tarballs, the tarball itself should also appear under artifacts with its sha256.

SBOM references (optional in v0)
- sbom
  - sbom_spdx_path (string) — relative path to a SPDX file (if included)
  - sbom_spdx_sha256 (string)
  - sbom_cyclonedx_path (string) — relative path (if included)
  - sbom_cyclonedx_sha256 (string)
  - v0 expectation: include at least one SBOM artifact for the release, or explicitly set sbom to "not_included" (string) with rationale.

Signing metadata (do we include in v0?)
- IMPORTANT: the signature itself is detached (manifest.sig). The manifest must not be self-referential.
- Question: do we include signer_key_id (kid) in the manifest?
  - Pros: easier debugging.
  - Cons: may complicate trust-store design / leakage.
- Proposed v0 (optional):
  - signing_key_id (string) — short identifier like "rw-rel-2025q4"
  - signing_algorithm (string) — e.g., "ed25519" or "ecdsa-p256"

Example manifest (v0) — illustrative only

{
  "manifest_format_version": "0.1",
  "bundle_id": "rbp_20260105_9f3a2c1_1842",
  "product": "redwood-private",
  "product_version": "2026.01.0",
  "build": "releases/private/2026.01.0+build.1842",
  "created_at": "2026-01-05T18:42:11Z",

  "requires_installer_version": ">=1.19.0",
  "requires_installer_features": "verify-signature,trust-store,downgrade-prevention",
  "upgrade_policy": "no-downgrade; install allowed from 2025.12.x -> 2026.01.x",
  "minimum_supported_product_version": "2025.12.0",

  "artifacts": [
    {
      "logical_name": "private-installer",
      "relative_path": "artifacts/redwood-private-installer_1.19.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz",
      "artifact_type": "installer",
      "sha256": "3d5f9a2d0b8c2f5f0c2d3b7f9bbf3d8b8e8b4d2c1a8d7e2f7a1c9e2d3f4a5b6c",
      "size_bytes": "18422133",
      "content_type": "application/gzip",
      "platform": "linux/amd64",
      "version": "1.19.0"
    },
    {
      "logical_name": "redwood-helm-charts",
      "relative_path": "artifacts/redwood-private-charts_2026.01.0.tgz",
      "artifact_type": "helm_chart",
      "sha256": "b2b3b4b5b6b7b8b9c0c1c2c3c4c5c6c7d8d9e0e1e2e3e4e5f6f7a8a9b0b1c2d3",
      "size_bytes": "9021431",
      "content_type": "application/gzip",
      "version": "2026.01.0"
    },
    {
      "logical_name": "runtime-artifacts",
      "relative_path": "artifacts/runtime/redwood-runtime_0.27.4.tar.zst",
      "artifact_type": "runtime",
      "sha256": "0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b",
      "size_bytes": "512334998",
      "content_type": "application/zstd",
      "version": "0.27.4"
    },
    {
      "logical_name": "sbom-spdx",
      "relative_path": "sbom/private_2026.01.0.spdx.json",
      "artifact_type": "sbom",
      "sha256": "9c9b9a9897969594939291908f8e8d8c8b8a898887868584838281807f7e7d7c7b",
      "size_bytes": "1442210",
      "content_type": "application/json"
    }
  ],

  "images": [
    {
      "name": "registry.redwood.example/redwood/control-plane",
      "digest": "sha256:111122223333444455556666777788889999aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff0000",
      "tags": "2026.01.0,latest-2026.01",
      "source": "redwood-release"
    }
  ],

  "sbom_spdx_path": "sbom/private_2026.01.0.spdx.json",
  "sbom_spdx_sha256": "9c9b9a9897969594939291908f8e8d8c8b8a898887868584838281807f7e7d7c7b"
}

Notes on example
- The manifest includes hashes for all files the installer will consume.
- The signature file (manifest.sig) is not included in artifacts and must never be.
- The image digest is separate from the tarball sha256; if we ship an image tarball, include it under artifacts and still list expected images for sanity checks.

Canonicalization + signing input (OPEN QUESTIONS)

1) Canonical JSON scheme
- We need stable signing bytes regardless of JSON serialization differences.
- Options:
  A) RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme)
     - Pros: standard-ish, multi-language implementations exist
     - Cons: implementation variability; need to confirm Go/Rust/TS libs maturity
  B) Define Redwood canonicalization rules (custom)
     - Rules would include: UTF-8, no insignificant whitespace, sort object keys lexicographically, arrays preserved in order, numeric normalization rules, escape handling.
     - Pros: tight control
     - Cons: risky to get wrong; more long-term maintenance
- Proposal for v0: adopt RFC 8785 if we can pick stable libs for installer languages; otherwise define minimal custom rules but document them extremely clearly.
- Action: check what languages we need canonicalization in (installer: Go; tooling: Python/Node; support CLI: Go).

2) YAML support?
- We’ve had repeated requests for YAML for operator readability.
- Concern: YAML has too many footguns (type inference, anchors, ordering) for signing.
- Proposal:
  - Canonical signed file is JSON only: manifest.json.
  - Optional manifest.yaml is generated for viewing only and is NOT signed and is explicitly marked as informational.
- If we do add YAML, the installer must ignore it (or treat it as a derived view).

3) Hash algorithms
- v0 currently uses sha256 for artifacts.
- Questions:
  - Do any customers require sha512? (some regulated environments prefer sha512-by-policy)
  - Do we need to support multiple hashes per artifact for migration (sha256 + sha512)?
- Proposal:
  - Keep sha256 as required; allow optional sha512 field.
  - If sha512 present, verification can check both (or prefer stronger) depending on policy.

4) Paths + normalization
- relative_path should be forward slashes always.
- Need to define:
  - No leading slash.
  - No .. segments.
  - UTF-8 normalization?
  - Case sensitivity expectations (Windows unpacking issues came up in pilots).

5) Size bytes type
- Using string to avoid overflow / JSON number parsing differences.
- Alternative is integer; but we’ve been burned by cross-language parsing and large files.

6) Artifact list ordering
- If we sign canonical JSON, artifact ordering should not affect signature if keys are sorted BUT array order still matters.
- Proposal:
  - Require artifacts array to be sorted by relative_path (or logical_name) during bundle generation.
  - Installer should not rely on ordering; but sorting makes diffs stable.

7) Downgrade prevention data
- minimum_supported_product_version may be insufficient if we need per-component minimums.
- Future: component_minimums as a map (but maps would be nested; we can still do in JSON but keep v0 simple).
- For now, installer can enforce:
  - product_version >= locally recorded installed_version OR allow explicit rollback flow (separate runbook).

8) What is “product_version” exactly?
- Redwood Private release tag vs chart version vs control plane build.
- Need one source of truth. My preference:
  - product_version maps to Private release train version (release notes)
  - charts/appVersion fields must align and can be separately recorded in artifacts entries.

Validation rules (v0)
- manifest_format_version must be recognized; unknown versions must fail closed unless operator uses a documented override (break-glass) and logs it.
- All required fields must be present.
- Every artifact referenced must exist in the bundle and match sha256 and size_bytes.
- No duplicate relative_path entries.
- All relative paths must be within the bundle root (prevent path traversal).

Installer UX expectations (notes for ENG-4823)
- On failure, error should report:
  - failing relative_path
  - expected sha256/size, observed sha256/size
  - guidance: “re-transfer bundle; do not edit/unzip/re-zip; verify checksums on transfer media”
- On success, print:
  - product_version, build, bundle_id
  - verification status and key id if available

Open questions / TODO
- Decide canonicalization approach (RFC 8785 vs custom) and document in ADR.
- Decide whether to include signing_key_id + signing_algorithm in the manifest.
- Confirm whether we can add optional sha512 alongside sha256.
- Confirm image inventory requirements for v0 (mandatory for GA? optional for pilot?).
- Add example for “detached signature file layout” once we align with installer PR (#24933).

Appendix: quick checklist for bundle generator (release pipeline)
- Generate artifacts list by walking bundle directories (excluding manifest.sig and any temp files).
- Compute sha256 + size deterministically.
- Sort artifacts by relative_path.
- Write manifest.json in canonical serialization.
- Sign canonical bytes; output manifest.sig.
- Run offline verification integration test (tamper tests) before publishing bundle.
